skill.name: jadx
skill.description: Use jadx to decompile Android APK files into readable Java source for authorized mobile security analysis.
skill.summary: Decompile Android APKs with jadx and review the resulting Java source for security issues.
skill.author: BrownFineSecurity

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, grep search patterns, and documentation examples in SKILL.md. One high-risk finding is confirmed because the skill recommends nmap-based network scanning, which is dual-use even when intended for authorized security work.

remediation.suggestion: Add explicit scope checks before any nmap or device enumeration step, and state that scans must stay within authorized targets.

remediation.issue: Credential testing workflow needs tighter guardrails
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that extracted credentials may only be validated in owned labs or approved assessments, and avoid instructions for unauthorized device access.

content.value_statement: Android APK security reviews are slow when bytecode and resources are hard to inspect. This skill guides jadx decompilation and focused source review for authorized assessments.
actual_capabilities: Guides basic and deobfuscated APK decompilation with jadx.
Explains when to use the jadx CLI or jadx GUI.
Provides search patterns for secrets, endpoints, storage, WebView, SQL, and crypto issues.
Shows batch processing workflows for multiple APK files.
Documents troubleshooting options for obfuscation, memory limits, and partial decompilation.
limitations: Requires jadx, Java, and enough local disk space to be installed before use.
Decompiled Java is approximate and may differ from the original source.
Does not prove exploitability without manual review and runtime validation.
Must only be used on APKs and systems the user is authorized to assess.

use_cases.title: Review a Mobile App for Secrets
use_cases.description: Decompile an APK and search source files for API keys, passwords, tokens, and exposed service URLs.

use_cases.title: Map Android App Behavior
use_cases.description: Inspect decompiled activities, services, receivers, and network clients to understand app logic and data flow.

use_cases.title: Investigate IoT Companion Apps
use_cases.description: Extract endpoints, authentication logic, and device discovery code from an authorized IoT mobile app review.

prompt_templates.title: Decompile One APK
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a single Android package.
prompt_templates.prompt: Decompile this APK with jadx, use deobfuscation if appropriate, and summarize the output layout.

prompt_templates.title: Find Hardcoded Secrets
prompt_templates.prompt: After decompilation, search the source and resources for hardcoded credentials, tokens, API keys, and service URLs.

prompt_templates.title: Review Security-Sensitive Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the decompiled code for insecure storage, weak crypto, WebView risks, SQL injection patterns, and certificate validation issues.

prompt_templates.title: Build an APK Analysis Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a repeatable jadx workflow for multiple APKs, including decompilation options, search strategy, triage steps, and validation notes.

output_examples.input: Analyze an APK for exposed credentials and endpoints.
output: Decompiled source location and resource location.
List of credential-like matches with file context.
Network endpoints grouped by host or service.
Recommended manual checks for false positives.

output_examples.input: Review an Android app for insecure crypto and storage patterns.
output: Summary of crypto APIs and algorithms found.
Storage mechanisms that may hold sensitive data.
Risk notes for weak algorithms or unsafe preferences.
Validation steps to confirm real exposure.

output_examples.input: Decompile several authorized APKs and summarize findings.
output: Search results grouped by issue type.

best_practices: Confirm authorization before decompiling an APK or testing extracted details.
Use deobfuscation for production apps, then verify important findings manually.
Pair jadx review with runtime testing before making security claims.
anti_patterns: Do not distribute decompiled source from third-party applications.
Do not treat grep matches as confirmed vulnerabilities without context.
Do not run network scans or credential tests outside the approved scope.

faq.question: What does this skill help analyze?
faq.answer: It helps decompile Android APK files with jadx and review the resulting Java source for security-relevant patterns.

faq.question: Does it install jadx automatically?
faq.answer: No. It assumes jadx, Java, and any optional companion tools are already installed by the user.

faq.question: Can it prove a vulnerability exists?
faq.answer: No. It can identify suspicious code patterns, but findings need manual review and runtime validation.

faq.question: Is jadx output the original source code?
faq.answer: No. Jadx reconstructs readable Java from bytecode, so names and logic may be incomplete or approximate.

faq.question: When should I use jadx-gui?
faq.answer: Use jadx-gui for interactive browsing, cross-references, and deeper review after initial command-line decompilation.

faq.question: What authorization is required?
faq.answer: Use it only on APKs and systems you own or have explicit permission to test.
